<?php

// phpcs:disable PSR1.Classes.ClassDeclaration.MissingNamespace

/**
 * THE ADAPTER THAT MAKES `BdSubmitOrderPlan` REACHABLE. Nothing else.
 *
 * `BdSubmitOrderPlan` has shipped in this package since rc33 and has been
 * INERT the whole time, by its own admission: *"Nothing in this package calls
 * plan(): the caller is core's `Submit to Order`, which belongs to another
 * lane."* ERP-Epicor `1.1.24-rc26` opened that lane -
 * `ErpQuoteHooks::fireResolveOrderableLines()` - and the union cut
 * `1.1.24-rc29` is the first ERP-Epicor label that carries it together with
 * the per-line `fireLineOrderRefusal()` seam this directory's sibling needs.
 * This file is the six lines that connect the two.
 *
 * ⛔ WITHOUT IT THE NARROWING IS INERT AND A BENCH LADDER SENDS EVERY RUNG -
 *    the shape that booked a $37,250 quote as a $47,950 order on Epicor 9209.
 *    The failure is SILENT: core's hook finds no file, returns the candidates
 *    unchanged, and the press succeeds.
 *
 * ================= WHY CORE CANNOT SHIP THIS FILE ITSELF =================
 *
 * It names `BdSubmitOrderPlan`, a class that exists only in this optional,
 * single-customer package. Naming it from the shared layer is exactly what
 * `ErpQuoteHooks` exists to avoid (gate G2, decision 102): the shared package
 * would carry a Bench Dogs symbol and a Bench Dogs rule would reach every
 * tenant. So the seam is core's and the adapter is the customer's, which is
 * the same division `ErpOpportunityLineRollupPolicy` already lives under.
 *
 * ========================= IT IS A PASS-THROUGH =========================
 *
 * Core's own contract asks for exactly that. `fireResolveOrderableLines()`
 * accepts TWO refusal spellings deliberately, and says why:
 *
 *     "Accepting it means the adapter such a package ships at this hook point
 *      is a PASS-THROUGH rather than a translation layer - and a translation
 *      layer between two refusal vocabularies is precisely where a refusal
 *      quietly becomes an empty list and an empty list quietly becomes
 *      'order everything'."
 *
 * `plan()` already answers in the second spelling
 * (`['line_ids' => [...], 'refusal' => ?string, 'error' => ?string]`), so this
 * file translates nothing, decides nothing, and authors no seller-facing words
 * except the one refusal below, which describes a BROKEN INSTALL and not a
 * business rule.
 *
 * 🚩 IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FILTER `$candidateLineIds`. Core intersects
 * `plan()`'s answer with its own candidate list and treats any id it did not
 * offer as a CONTRACT VIOLATION, which it turns into a refusal. Pre-filtering
 * here would convert that loud refusal into a silent narrowing - re-creating
 * the BD-05 duplicate-order class the intersection exists to catch. The
 * candidates are accepted, unread, on purpose.
 *
 * Same scanner-safe shape as the sibling providers in this directory: one
 * fixed literal path, one fixed class, one method, `file_exists()` before the
 * `require_once` (a `require_once` of a missing file is a compile fatal, not a
 * `\Throwable`, so core's catch would not see it), no glob, no dynamic
 * dispatch.
 */
class ErpQuoteResolveOrderableLinesHook
{
    /** The provider this adapter exists to reach. Fixed path, fixed class. */
    private const PLAN_FILE = 'custom/modules/Quotes/BdSubmitOrderPlan.php';

    /**
     * @param SugarBean $quote
     * @param string[] $candidateLineIds Live, not-yet-ordered line ids. Read by
     *                                   CORE, not by this adapter - see above.
     * @return array{line_ids: string[], refusal: ?string, error: ?string}
     */
    public function run($quote, array $candidateLineIds): array
    {
        // Same discipline as BdSubmitOrderPlan::loadSelector() and
        // ErpOrderSelectedLinesPolicy::loadSelector(): a half-installed
        // instance must not read as "no objection". Here that means REFUSING
        // rather than returning the candidates - returning them is what core
        // does when this file is absent, and a file that IS present but cannot
        // reach its planner has not said the lines are fine, it has said
        // nothing. Ordering the lot on the strength of that is the guess
        // decision 29 forbids, against irreversible ERP orders.
        if (!$this->loadPlanner()) {
            return array(
                'line_ids' => array(),
                'refusal' => 'The Bench Dogs order planner is not installed, so this quote cannot be '
                    . 'adjudicated and nothing was sent. Reinstall Bench Dogs Extensions, then try again.',
                'error' => 'Bench Dogs order planner is not installed',
            );
        }

        return (new BdSubmitOrderPlan())->plan($quote);
    }

    private function loadPlanner(): bool
    {
        if (class_exists('BdSubmitOrderPlan', false)) {
            return true;
        }
        if (!file_exists(self::PLAN_FILE)) {
            return false;
        }
        require_once self::PLAN_FILE;

        return class_exists('BdSubmitOrderPlan', false);
    }
}
